posts.author: mei
posts.text: Just finished the morning kiosk trial at Raffles Place (28 first-time users). 19 of them froze for over 2 minutes on Step 2 trying to guess 'Kopi O Kosong' vs 'Kopi C Siew Dai', and 72% missed the tiny language toggle in the corner.

posts.author: arjun
posts.text: Careful with renaming the POS buttons to English though. The kitchen docket currently prints the same button name the customer sees. When we tested 'Black Coffee No Sugar' at Tampines, our 65-year-old kopi uncles slowed down by 15 seconds a cup trying to read the docket. POS v2.4 can hold a separate kitchen print name, but it needs configuring and a kitchen test before 8am.

posts.author: mei
posts.text: Yeah, and Reddit roasted our rival down the street when they renamed Kopi O to 'Local Americano'. Plus the 15-inch screen only fits 12 buttons per page. Let's figure out what to change at the huddle.

posts.author: weiling
posts.text: Our 28 seats were jammed again this morning. Office workers left tissue packets on empty tables before joining the 15-min queue, and 4 laptop freelancers sat across our four 4-seater booths (16 seats) for 2 hours on a single $2.20 Kopi O. That's $420 in lost breakfast sets, and Auntie Mary (62) is still shaken after that guy in a suit yelled at her last week.

posts.author: arjun
posts.text: Those 12 booth wall plugs and the guest Wi-Fi router are wired to our smart relay breaker in the back room, and we still have the numbered table pucks in the storeroom. Let's bring it up in the meeting so we don't put Auntie Mary in the middle.

posts.author: daniel
posts.text: Heads up team: SFA just emailed an inspection notice for 9:00am tomorrow after a soft-trial diner was hospitalized with suspected salmonella (hospital lab results take 48 hours). Straits Times press arrives at 8:00am for our ribbon-cutting—should we pause soft-boiled eggs and put out a precautionary supplier batch #402 notice?

posts.author: weiling
posts.text: Hold on—our sous-vide holding bath dipped to 58°C for 45 minutes during yesterday's rush, and SFA food hygiene officers will swab the tank and check our temperature log at 9am. Pulling soft-boiled eggs wipes out 60% of breakfast sets ($1,800/morning), and we have two unopened cartons of pasteurized backup eggs (Batch #405) in the storeroom that can hold at 63°C. We still haven't decided our 9am SFA protocol or what we tell the 8am press.

posts.author: daniel
posts.text: GrabFood and Foodpanda just raised our CBD breakfast commission to 32%, so every $10 set delivered loses $0.40 after packaging. But platforms drive 50% of our morning sales ($2,400/morning) from CBD office towers—if we delist, those corporate orders go straight to Ya Kun.

posts.author: weiling
posts.text: And Arjun checked the POS: raising our single-set price on GrabFood by 30% to $13 triggers platform price-parity ranking penalties, while our direct web QR link only supports express self-pickup with no rider dispatch. We also can't pull floor staff off the counter to hand-deliver orders in CBD morning rain because of injury liability. We haven't agreed how to restructure our delivery menu or self-pickup perks yet.
